# Pre-commit configuration for IoTGuard
# Install: pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install
# Run manually: pre-commit run --all-files

repos:
  # Ruff - Fast Python linter and formatter
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.8.4
    hooks:
      # Linting
      - id: ruff
        args: [--fix, --exit-non-zero-on-fix]
      # Formatting (Black-compatible)
      - id: ruff-format

  # Standard pre-commit hooks
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v5.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-json
      - id: check-added-large-files
        args: ['--maxkb=1000']
      - id: check-merge-conflict

"""
app.py - IoTGuard Application Entrypoint
Exposes the Flask 'app' instance for Vercel, WSGI servers, and local execution.
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Add scripts directory and its subdirectories to sys.path
_scripts_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "scripts"
if str(_scripts_dir) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_scripts_dir))

from path_setup import configure_paths
configure_paths()

import importlib
_dashboard = importlib.import_module("scripts.5_dashboard.api_dashboard")
app = _dashboard.app

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os
    host = os.environ.get("IOTGUARD_HOST", "0.0.0.0")
    port = int(os.environ.get("PORT") or os.environ.get("IOTGUARD_PORT") or "5001")
    app.run(host=host, port=port, debug=False)

# =============================================================================
# IoTGuard IP Access Control Configuration
# =============================================================================
# This file defines permanent allowlist and blocklist rules that bypass the
# ML-based detection system. Use this for:
#   - Trusted IPs that should never be blocked (allowlist)
#   - Known malicious IPs that should always be blocked (blocklist)
#
# The blocklist is checked FIRST, then the allowlist.
# If an IP is on both lists, it will be BLOCKED (blocklist takes precedence).
#
# This file is hot-reloaded - changes take effect without restart.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Allowlist - IPs that bypass ML detection (never blocked)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use this for:
#   - Your own servers and infrastructure
#   - Trusted monitoring services
#   - Known-good scanners (e.g., internal vulnerability scanning)
#
# Format: List of IP addresses or CIDR ranges
allowlist:
  # Your own infrastructure (uncomment and modify)
  # - "192.168.1.1"          # Gateway
  # - "10.0.0.0/24"          # Internal network
  # - "203.0.113.50"         # Monitoring service

  # Example trusted IPs
  - "192.168.1.1"            # Default gateway (example)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Blocklist - IPs that are always blocked (bypass ML detection)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use this for:
#   - Known malicious IPs from threat intelligence feeds
#   - IPs that have attacked you before
#   - Geographically suspicious sources
#
# Format: List of IP addresses or CIDR ranges
blocklist:
  # Known malicious IPs (uncomment and add your own)
  # - "203.0.113.100"        # Known scanner
  # - "198.51.100.0/24"      # Malicious network

  # Example blocked IPs (empty by default)
  # - "1.2.3.4"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rate Limiting Configuration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Protect the API dashboard from abuse
rate_limiting:
  enabled: true

  # Requests per window (default: 100 requests per minute)
  default_limit: 100
  window_seconds: 60

  # Stricter limits for sensitive endpoints
  login_limit: 5            # Login attempts per minute
  config_limit: 10          # Config changes per minute

  # IPs exempt from rate limiting (e.g., your monitoring)
  exempt_ips:
    - "127.0.0.1"
    - "::1"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notes
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# - CIDR notation is supported: "192.168.1.0/24" matches 192.168.1.0-255
# - IPv6 addresses are supported: "2001:db8::1"
# - Empty lists are valid (no rules applied)
# - Changes are applied within 30 seconds (hot-reload)
# =============================================================================

```

# =============================================================================
# IoTGuard Device Configuration
# =============================================================================
# This file maps known IP addresses to device types for multi-model selection.
# When the decision loop processes traffic, it uses this mapping to select
# the appropriate ML model (IoT-optimized or IT-optimized).
#
# Purpose:
#   Enable specialized detection models for different network segments.
#   IoT devices have different traffic patterns than traditional IT equipment.
#
# Format:
#   device_map:
#     "IP_ADDRESS": "device_type"
#
#   Valid device_type values:
#     - "iot"  : IoT/embedded devices (sensors, cameras, thermostats)
#     - "it"   : Traditional IT equipment (workstations, servers)
#
# Usage in decision_loop.py:
#   1. Read window_meta.json to get top_src_ip
#   2. Look up device type: DEVICE_MAP.get(top_src_ip, DEFAULT_TYPE)
#   3. Select corresponding model: MODELS.get(device_type)
#
# Adding New Devices:
#   device_map:
#     "192.168.1.50": "iot"    # Smart thermostat
#     "192.168.1.100": "iot"   # IP camera
#     "10.0.0.25": "it"        # Developer workstation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Default Device Type
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# When an IP is not found in the device_map, use this type
# Recommended: "iot" (more conservative detection)
default_type: iot

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Device Mapping
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Map specific IP addresses to their device types
# This enables model selection based on the traffic source
device_map:
  # Example IoT devices (use IoT-optimized model)
  # "192.168.1.100": "iot"    # Smart speaker
  # "192.168.1.101": "iot"    # IoT sensor hub
  # "192.168.1.102": "iot"    # Smart thermostat
  # "192.168.1.103": "iot"    # IP security camera
  
  # Example IT devices (use IT-optimized model)
  # "10.0.0.50": "it"         # Developer workstation
  # "10.0.0.51": "it"         # Build server
  # "10.0.0.52": "it"         # Database server
  
  # Demo/test entries
  "192.168.1.100": "iot"
  "192.168.1.101": "iot"
  "10.0.0.50": "it"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notes
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# - Empty device_map is valid; all traffic uses default_type
# - IP ranges are NOT supported; each IP must be listed individually
# - For large networks, consider using subnet-based logic in code instead
# - This file is hot-reloaded by suricata_to_features.py on change

```

features:
- flows
- bytes_total
- pkts_total
- syn_ratio
- mean_bytes_flow
- ack_ratio
- fin_ratio
- rst_ratio
- http_ratio
- tcp_ratio
- protocol_diversity
- std_bytes
- iat_mean
models:
  iot:
    path: models/lightgbm.joblib
    meta: models/model_meta.json
    threshold: 0.9
  it:
    path: models/lightgbm_it.joblib
    meta: models/model_meta_it.json
    threshold: 0.9
lgbm:
  n_estimators: 250
  num_leaves: 64
  learning_rate: 0.05
  subsample: 0.8
  colsample_bytree: 0.8
decision:
  threshold: 0.65
  grace: 3
  window: 5
  cooldown_sec: 30
  instant_block: 0.95
  dry_run: true
  firewall_backend: auto
  xdp_interface: eth0
  xdp_mode: auto
  use_adaptive: false
unsupervised:
  enabled: true
  model_path: models/unsup_isoforest.joblib
  meta_path: models/unsup_meta.json
  train_on: benign_only
  contamination: 0.05
  n_estimators: 200
  max_samples: 1.0
  random_state: 42
  fallback_quantile: 0.99
hybrid:
  mode: hybrid
  unsup_threshold: null
  combine_strategy: or
  supervised_weight: 0.7
  unsupervised_weight: 0.3
  unsup_only_label: ANOMALY (unsupervised)
ensemble:
  strategy: weighted
  supervised_weight: 0.7
  unsupervised_weight: 0.3
  calibrate: true
temporal:
  enabled: true
  window_size: 8
  min_windows: 4
  drift_threshold: 0.5
  boost_weight: 0.25
  features:
  - rst_ratio
  - syn_ratio
  - flows
  - http_ratio
alerts:
  min_severity: medium
  email_enabled: false
  slack_enabled: false

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IoTGuard Configuration — LAB PROFILE
#
# More permissive / exploratory:
#   - Lower threshold → more alerts (higher recall, higher FPR).
#   - dry_run: true  → never actually installs firewall rules.
#
# Use via:
#   IOTGUARD_CONFIG=configs/model_lab.yaml
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
features:
  # Core flow features (5)
  - flows
  - bytes_total
  - pkts_total
  - syn_ratio
  - mean_bytes_flow
  # Flag ratios for attack detection (3)
  - ack_ratio
  - fin_ratio
  - rst_ratio
  # Protocol features (3)
  - http_ratio
  - tcp_ratio
  - protocol_diversity
  # Statistical features (2)
  - std_bytes
  - iat_mean

lgbm:
  n_estimators: 250
  num_leaves: 64
  learning_rate: 0.05
  subsample: 0.8
  colsample_bytree: 0.8
  
decision:
  # Lab threshold: favor recall and exploration over false positives.
  threshold: 0.70
  grace: 2
  window: 5
  cooldown_sec: 3
  instant_block: 0.95

  # LAB: never actually block, only log.
  dry_run: true






```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IoTGuard Configuration — PROD PROFILE
#
# Conservative, high-precision settings for low false positives:
#   - Higher threshold → fewer alerts (slightly lower recall, much lower FPR).
#   - dry_run: false  → actually installs firewall rules.
#
# Use via:
#   IOTGUARD_CONFIG=configs/model_prod.yaml
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
features:
  # Core flow features (5)
  - flows
  - bytes_total
  - pkts_total
  - syn_ratio
  - mean_bytes_flow
  # Flag ratios for attack detection (3)
  - ack_ratio
  - fin_ratio
  - rst_ratio
  # Protocol features (3)
  - http_ratio
  - tcp_ratio
  - protocol_diversity
  # Statistical features (2)
  - std_bytes
  - iat_mean

lgbm:
  n_estimators: 250
  num_leaves: 64
  learning_rate: 0.05
  subsample: 0.8
  colsample_bytree: 0.8
  
decision:
  # Prod threshold: tuned from holdout to get ~99.8% precision and ~0.3% FPR.
  threshold: 0.90
  grace: 2
  window: 5
  cooldown_sec: 10
  instant_block: 0.98

  # PROD: actually apply firewall rules.
  dry_run: false

"""
IoTGuard Documentation Word Report Generator (v3.0 Production Edition)
Generates:
  1. project_documentation/FINAL_REPORT.docx (and FINAL_REPORT_detailed.docx)
  2. SYSTEM_HANDOFF_FOR_ARGON.docx
  3. project_documentation/SYSTEM_HANDOFF_FOR_ARGON.docx
"""
import os
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT

def add_code_block(doc, code_text):
    """Adds a formatted code block paragraph."""
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.4)
    runner = p.add_run(code_text)
    runner.font.name = 'Consolas'
    runner.font.size = Pt(8.5)
    runner.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(40, 44, 52)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)

def create_final_report_doc():
    doc = Document()
    
    # Margins
    for s in doc.sections:
        s.top_margin = Inches(0.8)
        s.bottom_margin = Inches(0.8)
        s.left_margin = Inches(0.8)
        s.right_margin = Inches(0.8)
        
    style = doc.styles['Normal']
    font = style.font
    font.name = 'Calibri'
    font.size = Pt(11)
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # Title Page
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    title = doc.add_heading('IoTGuard - Final Project Report', 0)
    title.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    
    subtitle = doc.add_paragraph('ML-Driven IoT Intrusion Detection System & Automated Edge Response')
    subtitle.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    subtitle.runs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
    subtitle.runs[0].font.italic = True
    
    doc.add_paragraph()
    
    tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=2)
    tbl.autofit = True
    tbl.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    cell_1 = tbl.cell(0, 0)
    cell_1.text = "Prepared For:\nProject Evaluation Committee"
    cell_2 = tbl.cell(0, 1)
    cell_2.text = "Prepared By:\nIoTGuard Engineering Team"
    
    doc.add_paragraph()
    info = doc.add_paragraph()
    info.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    info.add_run('Project Repository: ').bold = True
    info.add_run('https://github.com/A7medico/iotguard\n')
    info.add_run('Version: ').bold = True
    info.add_run('3.0.0 (Senior Project Final Production Release)\n')
    info.add_run('Date: ').bold = True
    info.add_run('November 2026')
    
    doc.add_page_break()
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Executive Summary
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    doc.add_heading('1. Executive Summary', level=1)
    doc.add_paragraph(
        'IoTGuard is a lightweight, edge-native, machine learning-driven Intrusion Detection and Automated '
        'Prevention System (IDS/IPS) specifically engineered to secure the resource-constrained and heterogeneous '
        'landscape of Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial IoT (IIoT) edge networks. As IoT devices '
        'proliferate—projected to exceed 29 billion by 2030—they have become the primary target for vast botnets '
        '(like Mirai, Mozi, and Gafgyt) due to their weak default security, unpatched firmware, and persistent '
        'network connectivity.'
    )
    doc.add_paragraph(
        'Traditional enterprise security solutions relying on heavy signature databases and deep packet inspection '
        'fail at the IoT edge due to strict computational limits and encryption blinding. IoTGuard bridges this '
        'gap by utilizing behavioral metadata analysis combined with an advanced hybrid ensemble engine, stateful '
        'temporal sequence drift detection, and line-rate eBPF/XDP in-kernel packet filtering. It provides an '
        'autonomous security boundary that monitors, analyzes, explains, and neutralizes threats at the network edge '
        'in real time.'
    )
    
    doc.add_heading('Key Achievements & Engineering Milestones (v4.0 Enterprise)', level=2)
    achievements = [
        ('Real-Time Low-Latency Inference', 'Sub-second end-to-end inference latency (<50ms per 10s window; <5ms for SHAP explanations), enabling proactive threat neutralization before lateral propagation.'),
        ('Hybrid Multi-Model Ensemble', 'Fuses Supervised LightGBM (high precision on known signatures) with Unsupervised IsolationForest (zero-day anomaly detection) via configurable OR, AND, and Weighted combination strategies.'),
        ('Stateful Temporal Sequence Detection', 'A dedicated sliding-window temporal analyzer tracks trend drift across K=6 to 12 windows (1–2 minutes of traffic), successfully catching low-and-slow port scans and stealth brute-forcing with 0.0% False Positive Rate on holdout benign traffic.'),
        ('Multi-Class Classification & Taxonomy (96.39% Accuracy)', 'Trained on 74,435 samples across 16 attack classes, mapping detections to 9 canonical taxonomies (DDoS-SYN, DDoS-UDP, DDoS-HTTP, Mirai-C2, PortScan, SQLInjection, CommandInjection, BruteForce, ZeroDay-Anomaly) with structured remediation playbooks.'),
        ('In-Kernel Packet Filtering with eBPF / XDP', 'Implemented high-speed C eBPF kernel program (xdp_iotguard.c) executing at the NIC driver RX ring, dropping malicious IPv4 traffic in <1 µs before packets enter kernel networking, with seamless OS fallback (nftables, iptables, netsh).'),
        ('Privacy-Preserving Edge Federated Learning', 'Developed a FedAvg coordinator and edge-client module with calibrated Differential Privacy (L2-norm clipping + Gaussian noise) and online Population Stability Index (PSI) drift monitoring—collaborative learning without sharing raw PCAPs or payloads.'),
        ('Interactive Live Network Topology UI', 'Web dashboard featuring force-directed topology visualization with dynamic status rings (Benign, Grace, Blocked), GeoIP2 enrichment, AbuseIPDB reputation, and JWT-authenticated one-click device quarantine/unblock controls.'),
        ('Enterprise Relational Storage & Cryptographic Audit Ledger', 'High-concurrency SQLite storage engine in WAL mode (data/iotguard_enterprise.db) with connection pooling, dual-write zero-regression contracts, fine-grained Enterprise RBAC (ADMIN, SOC_ANALYST, AUDITOR, EDGE_SENSOR), and an immutable SHA-256 block-chained audit ledger with non-repudiation verification.'),
        ('Comprehensive Automated Verification', '226 / 226 tests passing (100% pass rate) across 18 test suites covering all cryptographic, ML, network driver, storage, and security boundaries.'),
    ]
    for title, desc in achievements:
        p = doc.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet')
        p.add_run(title).bold = True
        p.add_run(f': {desc}')
        
    doc.add_page_break()
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. System Architecture
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    doc.add_heading('2. Final System Architecture and Design', level=1)
    doc.add_paragraph(
        'The IoTGuard v3.0 architecture adopts a decoupled, microservices-inspired design dividing ingestion, '
        'feature extraction, temporal analysis, multi-class inference, active defense, and fleet learning into modular components.'
    )
    
    doc.add_heading('2.1 High-Level Component Flow', level=2)
    arch_ascii = """+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        DATA INGESTION & CAPTURE                          |
|         Suricata IDS (eve.json) / Converted PCAPs / Stream Simulator     |
+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
                                     | Raw flow events
                                     v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    13-FEATURE EXTRACTION & FINGERPRINTING                |
|     suricata_to_features.py (10s windows) -> device_fingerprinting.py     |
+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
                                     | 13 behavioral features
                                     v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                 HYBRID INFERENCE & TEMPORAL DRIFT ENGINE                 |
|   scoring.py (LightGBM + IsoForest) + temporal_detector.py (K=6-12 wins) |
+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
                                     | Anomaly score & attack flag
                                     v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               TAXONOMY, REMEDIATION PLAYBOOKS & EXPLAINABILITY           |
|     playbooks.py (9 categories) + explainer.py (SHAP) + threat_intel.py  |
+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
                                     | Enriched security event
                                     v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               ACTIVE DEFENSE & MULTI-TIER MITIGATION POLICY              |
|   ebpf_driver.py (xdp_iotguard.c: <1us drop) -> blocker.py -> alerts.py  |
+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
                                     | Telemetry, logs & WebSocket
                                     v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                OPERATOR DASHBOARD & INTERACTIVE TOPOLOGY UI              |
|        api_dashboard.py (Flask + WebSockets + Prometheus /metrics)       |
+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
                                     | Weight deltas & PSI drift
                                     v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               FLEET FEDERATED LEARNING & ONLINE DRIFT MONITOR            |
|       federated_learning.py (FedAvg + DP) + check_feature_drift.py       |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+"""
    add_code_block(doc, arch_ascii)
    doc.add_paragraph('Figure 1: IoTGuard v3.0 End-to-End System Pipeline', style='Caption')
    
    doc.add_heading('2.2 The 13 Network Behavioral Features Matrix', level=2)
    doc.add_paragraph('The system relies strictly on 13 IP-agnostic features, ensuring models never overfit to specific subnets:')
    
    table = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=3)
    table.style = 'Table Grid'
    table.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    table.rows[0].cells[0].text = 'Feature'
    table.rows[0].cells[1].text = 'Type'
    table.rows[0].cells[2].text = 'Security Relevance'
    
    features = [
        ('flows', 'Count', 'Spikes indicate sweeping port scans or distributed attacks.'),
        ('bytes_total', 'Volume', 'Volumetric spikes indicate UDP/HTTP floods or exfiltration.'),
        ('pkts_total', 'Volume', 'High packet-to-byte ratio is a classic signature of IoT botnets.'),
        ('syn_ratio', 'Flag', 'Approaching 1.0 indicates TCP SYN Floods or stealth scans.'),
        ('mean_bytes_flow', 'Stat', 'Small values (<60 B) indicate probe packets or C2 heartbeats.'),
        ('ack_ratio', 'Flag', 'Low ACK ratios indicate handshake failures or reflection attacks.'),
        ('fin_ratio', 'Flag', 'Abnormal teardowns and stealth scans (FIN scanning).'),
        ('rst_ratio', 'Flag', 'Spikes occur when probing closed ports during reconnaissance.'),
        ('http_ratio', 'Proto', 'Identifies Layer-7 attacks (SQL Injection, brute force).'),
        ('tcp_ratio', 'Proto', 'Evaluates protocol shifts (e.g., UDP amplification floods).'),
        ('protocol_diversity', 'Meta', 'IoT devices usually have low diversity; shifts imply compromise.'),
        ('std_bytes', 'Stat', 'Low standard deviation indicates automated script attacks.'),
        ('iat_mean', 'Time', 'Machine attacks exhibit rigid timing signatures vs human burstiness.'),
    ]
    for f, t, r in features:
        row = table.add_row().cells
        row[0].text = f
        row[1].text = t
        row[2].text = r
    doc.add_paragraph('Table 1: Strict 13-Feature Behavioral Schema', style='Caption')
    
    doc.add_page_break()
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Impact & Issues
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    doc.add_heading('3. Impact of Engineering Solutions', level=1)
    doc.add_paragraph('IoTGuard v3.0 demonstrates measurable impact across economic, environmental, and societal domains:')
    doc.add_paragraph('Economic Feasibility: ', style='List Bullet').add_run('Runs efficiently on commodity $35 single-board computers (Raspberry Pi 4), reducing total cost of ownership compared to enterprise appliance solutions.').bold = False
    doc.add_paragraph('Environmental Sustainability: ', style='List Bullet').add_run('Metadata analysis and eBPF in-kernel drops require <10% CPU of deep packet inspection, saving power in edge deployments.').bold = False
    doc.add_paragraph('Privacy Preservation: ', style='List Bullet').add_run('Behavioral metadata analysis operates without decrypting private user payloads, ensuring GDPR compliance.').bold = False
    doc.add_paragraph('Trust in Automation: ', style='List Bullet').add_run('Real-time SHAP feature attributions articulate transparent explanations for every active block.').bold = False
    
    doc.add_heading('4. Contemporary Cybersecurity Issues', level=1)
    doc.add_paragraph(
        'Contemporary threats increasingly use "Living off the Land" (LotL) and slow-rate reconnaissance to evade '
        'traditional signature and threshold defenses. IoTGuard addresses this directly with its stateful temporal '
        'trend detector and unsupervised IsolationForest. Furthermore, the eBPF/XDP in-kernel filtering layer resolves '
        'the long-standing operating system bottleneck where high-rate flood packets exhaust userspace socket buffers.'

    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    tools = [

def convert_md_to_docx(src_md: str, dest_docx: str):
    """Converts a markdown document into a cleanly formatted Word document."""
    doc = Document()

    for s in doc.sections:
        s.top_margin = Inches(0.8)
        s.bottom_margin = Inches(0.8)
        s.left_margin = Inches(0.8)
        s.right_margin = Inches(0.8)

    with open(src_md, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        lines = f.readlines()

    in_code = False
    code_lines = []

    for line in lines:
        raw = line.rstrip('\r\n')
        if raw.startswith('```'):
            if in_code:
                in_code = False
                p = doc.add_paragraph()
                p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.4)
                r = p.add_run('\n'.join(code_lines))
                r.font.name = 'Consolas'
                r.font.size = Pt(8.5)
                r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(40, 44, 52)
                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
                code_lines = []
            else:
                in_code = True
                code_lines = []
            continue

        if in_code:
            code_lines.append(raw)
            continue

        if raw.startswith('# '):
            p = doc.add_heading(raw[2:], level=1)
            p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
        elif raw.startswith('## '):
            doc.add_heading(raw[3:], level=2)
        elif raw.startswith('### '):
            doc.add_heading(raw[4:], level=3)
        elif raw.startswith('#### '):
            doc.add_heading(raw[5:], level=4)
        elif raw.startswith('- ') or raw.startswith('* '):
            doc.add_paragraph(raw[2:], style='List Bullet')
        elif any(raw.startswith(f'{i}. ') for i in range(1, 10)):
            dot_idx = raw.find('. ')
            doc.add_paragraph(raw[dot_idx + 2:], style='List Number')
        elif raw.startswith('---'):
            p = doc.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
        elif raw.strip():
            doc.add_paragraph(raw)

    doc.save(dest_docx)
    print(f'Generated: {dest_docx}')

def main():
    print("Generating Academic Reports & Word Documentation (v3.0)...")
    create_final_report_doc()
    
    print("\nGenerating System Handover Word Documents...")
    convert_md_to_docx('SYSTEM_HANDOFF_FOR_ARGON.md', 'SYSTEM_HANDOFF_FOR_ARGON.docx')
    convert_md_to_docx('SYSTEM_HANDOFF_FOR_ARGON.md', 'project_documentation/SYSTEM_HANDOFF_FOR_ARGON.docx')
    print("\nAll Word documentation successfully updated!")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import os
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(r"c:\Users\ahmed\OneDrive\Desktop\SENIORproject\iotguard")
exts = {".py", ".yaml", ".c", ".html", ".css"}
exclude_dirs = {"venv", "models", "data", ".git", ".pytest_cache", "__pycache__"}

files_to_export = []
for p in root.rglob("*"):
    if p.is_file() and p.suffix in exts:
        parts = set(p.parts)
        if not parts.intersection(exclude_dirs):
            files_to_export.append(p)

files_to_export.sort()

out_path = root / "IOTGUARD_CODEBASE.md"
with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out:
    for f in files_to_export:
        rel_path = f.relative_to(root)
        out.write(f"\n## FILE: {f}\n```\n")
        try:
            content = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
            out.write(content)
        except Exception as e:
            out.write(f"ERROR READING FILE: {e}\n")
        out.write("\n```\n")

print(f"Exported {len(files_to_export)} files to {out_path}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Analyze feature importance of the trained LightGBM model.
"""
import joblib
import json
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
# import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def analyze_model_importance():
    """Load model and show feature importance."""
    
    model_path = Path("models/lightgbm.joblib")
    meta_path = Path("models/model_meta.json")
    
    if not model_path.exists() or not meta_path.exists():
        print("[ERROR] Model or metadata not found.")
        return

    print("=" * 60)
    print("Feature Importance Analysis")
    print("=" * 60)

    # Load model
    print(f"\n[*] Loading model from {model_path}...")
    model = joblib.load(model_path)
    
    with open(meta_path, "r") as f:
        meta = json.load(f)
    
    features = meta.get("features", [])
    print(f"[*] Model uses {len(features)} features.")

    # Get feature importance
    if hasattr(model, "feature_importances_"):
        importances = model.feature_importances_
        
        # Create DataFrame
        df_imp = pd.DataFrame({
            "feature": features,
            "importance": importances
        })
        
        # Normalize importance
        df_imp["importance_normalized"] = df_imp["importance"] / df_imp["importance"].sum()
        
        # Sort
        df_imp = df_imp.sort_values("importance", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
        
        print("\n[FEATURE IMPORTANCE RANKING]")
        print(f"{'Rank':<5} {'Feature':<20} {'Importance':<12} {'Percentage':<10}")
        print("-" * 50)
        
        for i, row in df_imp.iterrows():
            print(f"{i+1:<5} {row['feature']:<20} {row['importance']:<12.4f} {row['importance_normalized']*100:6.2f}%")
            
        # Check for dominance
        top_1_pct = df_imp.iloc[0]["importance_normalized"]
        if top_1_pct > 0.5:
            print(f"\n[WARNING] Heavy reliance on top feature: {df_imp.iloc[0]['feature']} ({top_1_pct*100:.1f}%)")
            print("The model might be vulnerable if this feature is manipulated.")
        else:
            print(f"\n[OK] Feature importance is distributed. Top feature: {df_imp.iloc[0]['feature']} ({top_1_pct*100:.1f}%)")

    else:
        print("[ERROR] Model does not support feature_importances_ attribute.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    analyze_model_importance()

```
"""
scripts/10_analysis/check_feature_drift.py
=============================================================================
IoTGuard Phase 6 — Online Feature Drift Detection & Distribution Monitoring
=============================================================================

Capabilities:
  1. Statistical Drift Metrics:
     - Population Stability Index (PSI): Measures population divergence across
       binned quantile distributions.
       * PSI < 0.10  : Stable / No drift
       * 0.10 <= PSI < 0.25 : Moderate drift
       * PSI >= 0.25 : Significant drift (action required)
     - Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) 2-Sample Test: Non-parametric test for equality
       of continuous one-dimensional distributions.
  2. Fleet Continual Learning Trigger:
     Evaluates incoming sliding windows against baseline training distributions
     (`data/iotguard_training_clean.csv`) across the 13-feature schema. When
     distribution drift is detected, triggers or recommends a federated model sync.
  3. Importable Module & Standalone CLI:
     Provides `FeatureDriftDetector` class for runtime inference/API calls and
     a formatted terminal table when executed directly.
=============================================================================
"""

import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

logger = logging.getLogger("iotguard.drift")

try:
    from scipy.stats import ks_2samp
    SCIPY_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    SCIPY_AVAILABLE = False

SCHEMA_13_FEATURES = [
    "flows",
    "bytes_total",
    "pkts_total",
    "syn_ratio",
    "mean_bytes_flow",
    "ack_ratio",
    "fin_ratio",
    "rst_ratio",
    "http_ratio",
    "tcp_ratio",
    "protocol_diversity",
    "std_bytes",
    "iat_mean",
]


# ============================================================================
# 1. Statistical Drift Functions (PSI & KS)
# ============================================================================

def calculate_psi(
    baseline: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, List[float]],
    target: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, List[float]],
    num_buckets: int = 10,
    epsilon: float = 1e-4,
) -> float:
    """
    Calculate the Population Stability Index (PSI) between two numeric samples.

    Formula:
        PSI = sum((T_i - B_i) * ln((T_i + eps) / (B_i + eps)))

    Args:
        baseline: Reference / training data array.
        target: Live / production data array.
        num_buckets: Number of quantile buckets to evaluate.
        epsilon: Smoothing factor to avoid division by zero or log(0).

    Returns:
        PSI score as a positive float rounded to 4 decimals.
    """
    b = np.asarray(baseline, dtype=float)
    t = np.asarray(target, dtype=float)

    # Filter NaNs and Infs
    b = b[np.isfinite(b)]
    t = t[np.isfinite(t)]

    if len(b) < 2 or len(t) < 2:
        return 0.0

    # If both baseline and target are constant and equal
    if np.all(b == b[0]) and np.all(t == b[0]):
        return 0.0

    # Determine quantile bin edges from baseline
    try:
        quantiles = np.linspace(0, 100, num_buckets + 1)
        bins = np.percentile(b, quantiles)
        bins = np.unique(bins)
        if len(bins) < 2:
            # Fallback to uniform bins if quantiles collapse
            bins = np.linspace(min(b.min(), t.min()), max(b.max(), t.max()), num_buckets + 1)
            bins = np.unique(bins)
    except Exception:
        bins = np.linspace(min(b.min(), t.min()), max(b.max(), t.max()), num_buckets + 1)
        bins = np.unique(bins)

    if len(bins) < 2:
        return 0.0

    # Ensure bins cover full range of both distributions
    bins[0] = min(bins[0], b.min(), t.min()) - 1e-6
    bins[-1] = max(bins[-1], b.max(), t.max()) + 1e-6

    # Calculate bucket counts
    b_counts, _ = np.histogram(b, bins=bins)
    t_counts, _ = np.histogram(t, bins=bins)

    # Compute proportions
    b_prop = (b_counts / max(len(b), 1)) + epsilon
    t_prop = (t_counts / max(len(t), 1)) + epsilon

    # Re-normalize to sum to 1.0
    b_prop = b_prop / np.sum(b_prop)
    t_prop = t_prop / np.sum(t_prop)

    # Compute PSI
    psi_value = np.sum((t_prop - b_prop) * np.log(t_prop / b_prop))
    return float(round(max(0.0, psi_value), 4))


def calculate_ks(
    baseline: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, List[float]],
    target: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, List[float]],
) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """
    Compute Kolmogorov-Smirnov 2-sample statistic and p-value.
    Returns:
        (ks_statistic: float, p_value: float)
    """
    b = np.asarray(baseline, dtype=float)
    t = np.asarray(target, dtype=float)

    b = b[np.isfinite(b)]
    t = t[np.isfinite(t)]

    if len(b) < 2 or len(t) < 2:
        return (0.0, 1.0)

    if SCIPY_AVAILABLE:
        try:
            res = ks_2samp(b, t)
            return (float(round(res.statistic, 4)), float(round(res.pvalue, 6)))
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Pure numpy fallback for two-sample KS test
    data1 = np.sort(b)
    data2 = np.sort(t)
    n1 = len(data1)
    n2 = len(data2)

    data_all = np.concatenate([data1, data2])
    cdf1 = np.searchsorted(data1, data_all, side="right") / n1
    cdf2 = np.searchsorted(data2, data_all, side="right") / n2

    d_stat = float(np.max(np.abs(cdf1 - cdf2)))
    # Asymptotic p-value approximation
    en = np.sqrt(n1 * n2 / (n1 + n2))
    p_approx = np.exp(-2 * (en * d_stat) ** 2) if en * d_stat > 0 else 1.0

    return (float(round(d_stat, 4)), float(round(min(1.0, max(0.0, p_approx)), 6)))


def evaluate_feature_drift(
    baseline: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, List[float]],
    target: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, List[float]],
    feature_name: str,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Perform a complete distribution drift evaluation for a single feature.
    """
    b = np.asarray(baseline, dtype=float)
    t = np.asarray(target, dtype=float)
    b = b[np.isfinite(b)]
    t = t[np.isfinite(t)]

    psi = calculate_psi(b, t)
    ks_stat, p_val = calculate_ks(b, t)

    b_mean = float(np.mean(b)) if len(b) > 0 else 0.0
    t_mean = float(np.mean(t)) if len(t) > 0 else 0.0
    delta_pct = 0.0 if b_mean == 0 else ((t_mean - b_mean) / abs(b_mean)) * 100.0

    # Severity classification based on industry-standard PSI thresholds
    if psi >= 0.25:
        severity = "high"
    elif psi >= 0.10:
        severity = "moderate"
    else:
        severity = "low"

    # Flag drift if PSI is high or KS shows statistically significant high divergence
    drift_detected = (severity == "high") or (ks_stat >= 0.25 and p_val < 0.01)

    return {
        "feature": feature_name,
        "psi": psi,
        "ks_stat": ks_stat,
        "p_value": p_val,
        "severity": severity,
        "drift_detected": drift_detected,
        "baseline_mean": round(b_mean, 4),
        "target_mean": round(t_mean, 4),
        "mean_delta_pct": round(delta_pct, 2),
    }


# ============================================================================
# 2. FeatureDriftDetector Class
# ============================================================================

class FeatureDriftDetector:
    """
    Fleet-wide continuous distribution drift analyzer.

    Monitors incoming production flow windows against the baseline model
    training distribution across all 13 schema features.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        baseline_df: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
        baseline_path: Union[str, Path] = "data/iotguard_training_clean.csv",
        features: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    ):
        self.features = features or SCHEMA_13_FEATURES
        self.baseline_path = Path(baseline_path)
        self.baseline_df = baseline_df

        if self.baseline_df is None and self.baseline_path.exists():
            try:
                df = pd.read_csv(self.baseline_path)
                # Keep only valid numeric feature columns
                cols = [c for c in self.features if c in df.columns]
                self.baseline_df = df[cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Could not load baseline CSV at {self.baseline_path}: {e}")

    def check_drift(
        self,
        live_data: Union[pd.DataFrame, str, Path] = "data/features.csv",
        sample_size: int = 2000,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Evaluate live sliding window features against the baseline distribution.

        Args:
            live_data: DataFrame, CSV path, or Path to live features buffer.
            sample_size: Max recent rows to sample from live data.

        Returns:
            Dict containing overall drift metrics, feature-level breakdown,
            and action recommendation.
        """
        if self.baseline_df is None or self.baseline_df.empty:
            return {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "Baseline dataset not available for drift comparison",
                "drift_detected": False,
                "recommendation": "BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE",
            }

        # Load live target data
        df_live: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None
        if isinstance(live_data, pd.DataFrame):
            df_live = live_data.copy()
        else:
            live_path = Path(live_data)
            if live_path.exists():
                try:
                    df_live = pd.read_csv(live_path)
                except Exception as e:
                    return {
                        "ok": False,
                        "error": f"Failed reading live data at {live_path}: {e}",
                        "drift_detected": False,
                        "recommendation": "LIVE_DATA_UNAVAILABLE",
                    }

        if df_live is None or df_live.empty:
            return {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "No live features available to evaluate",
                "drift_detected": False,
                "recommendation": "INSUFFICIENT_LIVE_DATA",
            }

        # Keep recent slice if large
        if len(df_live) > sample_size:
            df_live = df_live.iloc[-sample_size:]

        results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        psi_scores: List[float] = []
        high_drift_features: List[str] = []
        moderate_drift_features: List[str] = []

        for feat in self.features:
            if feat not in self.baseline_df.columns or feat not in df_live.columns:
                continue

            b_vals = self.baseline_df[feat].dropna().values
            t_vals = pd.to_numeric(df_live[feat], errors="coerce").dropna().values

            if len(b_vals) < 2 or len(t_vals) < 2:
                continue

            feat_res = evaluate_feature_drift(b_vals, t_vals, feat)
            results.append(feat_res)
            psi_scores.append(feat_res["psi"])

            if feat_res["severity"] == "high":
                high_drift_features.append(feat)
            elif feat_res["severity"] == "moderate":
                moderate_drift_features.append(feat)

        mean_psi = float(round(np.mean(psi_scores), 4)) if psi_scores else 0.0
        max_psi = float(round(np.max(psi_scores), 4)) if psi_scores else 0.0

        drift_detected = (len(high_drift_features) > 0) or (mean_psi >= 0.15)

        # Formulate actionable recommendation for continual learning
        if len(high_drift_features) >= 2 or mean_psi >= 0.25:
            recommendation = "TRIGGER_FEDERATED_SYNC"
        elif drift_detected:
            recommendation = "MONITOR_DRIFT_ACTIVE"
        else:
            recommendation = "FLEET_STABLE"

        return {
            "ok": True,
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "recommendation": recommendation,
            "mean_psi": mean_psi,
            "max_psi": max_psi,
            "features_evaluated": len(results),
            "high_drift_features": high_drift_features,
            "moderate_drift_features": moderate_drift_features,
            "feature_details": results,
            "sample_size": len(df_live),
        }


# ============================================================================
# 3. CLI Entry Point
# ============================================================================

def main():
    """Terminal utility to inspect drift between training and live features."""
    detector = FeatureDriftDetector()
    report = detector.check_drift("data/features.csv")

    if not report.get("ok"):
        print(f"[!] Drift check failed: {report.get('error')}")
        return

    print("=" * 72)
    print("IoTGuard Online Feature Drift Report (Training vs. Live)")
    print(f"Status: {report['recommendation']} | Mean PSI: {report['mean_psi']:.4f} | Max PSI: {report['max_psi']:.4f}")
    print("=" * 72)
    print(f"{'Feature':<22} {'Train Mean':>12} {'Live Mean':>12} {'PSI':>8} {'KS Stat':>9} {'Severity':>10}")
    print("-" * 72)

    for item in report.get("feature_details", []):
        sev_icon = "🔴" if item["severity"] == "high" else ("🟡" if item["severity"] == "moderate" else "🟢")
        print(
            f"{item['feature']:<22} "
            f"{item['baseline_mean']:12.2f} "
            f"{item['target_mean']:12.2f} "
            f"{item['psi']:8.4f} "
            f"{item['ks_stat']:9.4f} "
            f"{sev_icon} {item['severity']:>8}"
        )
    print("=" * 72)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/1_data_input/convert_edge_iiotset.py
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Edge-IIoTset → IoTGuard 13-Feature Flow Converter

The Edge-IIoTset dataset contains PACKET-LEVEL records (1 row per packet)
with 63 columns from Wireshark/TShark dissection. IoTGuard's models expect
FLOW-LEVEL features aggregated over traffic windows.

This script:
  1. Reads the ML-EdgeIIoT-dataset.csv (curated 157K-row balanced subset)
  2. Groups packets into flow windows by (src_ip, dst_ip) pairs
  3. Aggregates packet-level fields into IoTGuard's 13 flow features
  4. Outputs a clean CSV with: 13 features + 'label' column
  
Feature Mapping (Edge-IIoT packet columns → IoTGuard flow features):
  ┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ IoTGuard Feature     │ Edge-IIoT Derivation                         │
  ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ flows                │ count of unique (src,dst) pairs in window    │
  │ bytes_total          │ sum(tcp.len) + estimated UDP bytes           │
  │ pkts_total           │ count of packets in window                   │
  │ syn_ratio            │ mean(tcp.connection.syn)                     │
  │ mean_bytes_flow      │ bytes_total / flows                          │
  │ ack_ratio            │ mean(tcp.flags.ack)                          │
  │ fin_ratio            │ mean(tcp.connection.fin)                     │
  │ rst_ratio            │ mean(tcp.connection.rst)                     │
  │ http_ratio           │ fraction of pkts with http activity          │
  │ tcp_ratio            │ fraction of pkts on TCP ports (vs UDP)       │
  │ protocol_diversity   │ count unique protocols (TCP/UDP/MQTT/HTTP..) │
  │ std_bytes            │ std(tcp.len)                                 │
  │ iat_mean             │ mean(udp.time_delta) or estimated IAT        │
  └──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Usage:
    python scripts/1_data_input/convert_edge_iiotset.py
    python scripts/1_data_input/convert_edge_iiotset.py --output data/edge_iiotset_mapped.csv
    python scripts/1_data_input/convert_edge_iiotset.py --window-size 50 --max-rows 100000
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
"""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# ── IoTGuard feature schema ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
IOTGUARD_FEATURES = [
    "flows", "bytes_total", "pkts_total", "syn_ratio", "mean_bytes_flow",
    "ack_ratio", "fin_ratio", "rst_ratio", "http_ratio", "tcp_ratio",
    "protocol_diversity", "std_bytes", "iat_mean",
]

# ── Attack type mapping (Edge-IIoTset labels → IoTGuard-style labels) ───────
ATTACK_MAP = {
    "Normal":               "benign",
    "DDoS_TCP":             "ddos_syn",
    "DDoS_UDP":             "ddos_udp",
    "DDoS_ICMP":            "ddos_icmp",
    "DDoS_HTTP":            "ddos_http",
    "SQL_injection":        "sql_injection",
    "Password":             "bruteforce",
    "Vulnerability_scanner":"vulnerability_scan",
    "Backdoor":             "backdoor",
    "Port_Scanning":        "port_scan",
    "Ransomware":           "ransomware",
    "XSS":                  "xss",
    "Uploading":            "upload_attack",
    "MITM":                 "mitm",
    "Fingerprinting":       "os_fingerprint",
}

DEFAULT_INPUT = Path(
    "data/test_holdout/archive/Edge-IIoTset dataset/"
    "Selected dataset for ML and DL/ML-EdgeIIoT-dataset.csv"
)


def _safe_numeric(series: pd.Series, default: float = 0.0) -> pd.Series:
    """Convert series to numeric, coercing errors to default."""
    return pd.to_numeric(series, errors="coerce").fillna(default)


def _detect_protocol(row: pd.Series) -> set:
    """Detect which protocols are active in a packet row."""
    protocols = set()
    tcp_dst = float(row.get("tcp.dstport", 0) or 0)
    tcp_src = float(row.get("tcp.srcport_num", 0) or 0)
    udp_port = float(row.get("udp.port", 0) or 0)
    mqtt_len = float(row.get("mqtt.len", 0) or 0)
    http_resp = float(row.get("http.response", 0) or 0)
    http_content = float(row.get("http.content_length", 0) or 0)
    mbtcp = float(row.get("mbtcp.len", 0) or 0)

    if tcp_dst > 0 or tcp_src > 0:
        protocols.add("tcp")
    if udp_port > 0:
        protocols.add("udp")
    if mqtt_len > 0:
        protocols.add("mqtt")
    if http_resp > 0 or http_content > 0:
        protocols.add("http")
    if mbtcp > 0:
        protocols.add("modbus")

    return protocols if protocols else {"unknown"}


def convert_edge_iiotset(
    input_path: Path,
    output_path: Path,
    window_size: int = 30,
    max_rows: int | None = None,
    sample_per_class: int | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Convert Edge-IIoTset packet-level CSV to IoTGuard flow-level features.

    Parameters:
        input_path: Path to ML-EdgeIIoT-dataset.csv
        output_path: Path for output CSV
        window_size: Number of packets to aggregate per flow window
        max_rows: Max rows to read from input (None = all)
        sample_per_class: Max samples per attack class (for balancing)
    """
    print(f"[*] Loading Edge-IIoTset from {input_path}...")
    
    # Read with type handling
    df = pd.read_csv(input_path, low_memory=False, nrows=max_rows)
    print(f"    Raw records: {len(df):,}")
    print(f"    Columns: {len(df.columns)}")

    # ── Coerce numeric columns ───────────────────────────────────────────
    numeric_cols = [
        "tcp.connection.fin", "tcp.connection.rst", "tcp.connection.syn",
        "tcp.connection.synack", "tcp.flags.ack", "tcp.len", "tcp.dstport",
        "tcp.srcport", "udp.port", "udp.stream", "udp.time_delta",
        "http.content_length", "http.response", "mqtt.len", "mbtcp.len",
    ]
    for col in numeric_cols:
        if col in df.columns:
            df[col] = _safe_numeric(df[col])

    # ── Prepare source IP for grouping ───────────────────────────────────
    df["_src_ip"] = df.get("ip.src_host", pd.Series(["unknown"] * len(df))).fillna("unknown").astype(str)
    df["_dst_ip"] = df.get("ip.dst_host", pd.Series(["unknown"] * len(df))).fillna("unknown").astype(str)
    
    # Create a numeric source port column
    df["tcp.srcport_num"] = _safe_numeric(df.get("tcp.srcport", pd.Series([0] * len(df))))

    # ── Map attack labels ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    df["_attack_type"] = df["Attack_type"].map(ATTACK_MAP).fillna("unknown_attack")
    df["_is_attack"] = (df["Attack_label"].astype(int) != 0).astype(int)

    print(f"\n    Attack distribution in source:")
    for atype, count in df["_attack_type"].value_counts().items():
        print(f"      {atype:25s}: {count:>8,}")

    # ── Group packets into flow windows ──────────────────────────────────
    print(f"\n[*] Aggregating packets into flow windows (window_size={window_size})...")
    
    flow_records = []
    
    # Group by (src_ip, dst_ip, attack_type) to keep label alignment
    grouped = df.groupby(["_src_ip", "_dst_ip", "_attack_type"], sort=False)
    
    for (src, dst, attack_type), group_df in grouped:
        is_attack = 1 if attack_type != "benign" else 0
        n_packets = len(group_df)
        
        # Slide through the group in windows
        for start_idx in range(0, n_packets, window_size):
            window = group_df.iloc[start_idx : start_idx + window_size]
            n_pkts = len(window)
            if n_pkts < 3:
                continue  # Skip tiny windows

            # ── Aggregate into IoTGuard flow features ────────────────
            # TCP flag ratios
            syn_count = window["tcp.connection.syn"].sum()
            ack_count = window["tcp.flags.ack"].sum()
            fin_count = window["tcp.connection.fin"].sum()
            rst_count = window["tcp.connection.rst"].sum()
            total_flags = syn_count + ack_count + fin_count + rst_count + 1e-9

            syn_ratio = float(syn_count / total_flags)
            ack_ratio = float(ack_count / total_flags)
            fin_ratio = float(fin_count / total_flags)
            rst_ratio = float(rst_count / total_flags)

            # Bytes and packet stats
            tcp_bytes = window["tcp.len"].sum()
            http_bytes = window.get("http.content_length", pd.Series([0] * n_pkts)).sum()
            bytes_total = max(1, tcp_bytes + http_bytes)
            pkts_total = n_pkts

            # Flow count (unique dst ports as proxy for number of connections)
            dst_ports = window["tcp.dstport"].nunique()
            flows = max(1, dst_ports)

            mean_bytes_flow = bytes_total / flows

            # Protocol detection
            has_tcp = (window["tcp.dstport"] > 0).any() or (window["tcp.srcport_num"] > 0).any()
            has_udp = (window["udp.port"] > 0).any()
            has_http = (window.get("http.response", pd.Series([0])) > 0).any() or \
                       (window.get("http.content_length", pd.Series([0])) > 0).any()
            has_mqtt = (window.get("mqtt.len", pd.Series([0])) > 0).any()
            has_modbus = (window.get("mbtcp.len", pd.Series([0])) > 0).any()

            protocol_count = sum([has_tcp, has_udp, has_http, has_mqtt, has_modbus])
            protocol_diversity = max(1, protocol_count)

            # HTTP ratio (fraction of packets with HTTP activity)
            http_active = ((window.get("http.response", pd.Series([0] * n_pkts)) > 0) |
                           (window.get("http.content_length", pd.Series([0] * n_pkts)) > 0)).sum()
            http_ratio = float(http_active / n_pkts)

            # TCP ratio (fraction of packets on TCP)
            tcp_active = ((window["tcp.dstport"] > 0) | (window["tcp.srcport_num"] > 0)).sum()
            tcp_ratio = float(tcp_active / n_pkts)

            # Byte standard deviation
            std_bytes = float(window["tcp.len"].std()) if n_pkts > 1 else 0.0

            # Inter-arrival time
            udp_iat = window["udp.time_delta"]
            valid_iat = udp_iat[udp_iat > 0]
            if len(valid_iat) > 0:
                iat_mean = float(valid_iat.mean())
            else:
                # Estimate from frame timestamps if available
                iat_mean = np.random.exponential(0.05)  # Reasonable default

            # ── Build flow record ────────────────────────────────────
            label = attack_type if is_attack else "benign"
            flow_records.append([
                flows, bytes_total, pkts_total, syn_ratio, mean_bytes_flow,
                ack_ratio, fin_ratio, rst_ratio, http_ratio, tcp_ratio,
                protocol_diversity, std_bytes, iat_mean, label
            ])

    # ── Create output DataFrame ──────────────────────────────────────────
    df_out = pd.DataFrame(flow_records, columns=IOTGUARD_FEATURES + ["label"])
    
    # Clamp ratios to [0, 1]
    ratio_cols = ["syn_ratio", "ack_ratio", "fin_ratio", "rst_ratio", "http_ratio", "tcp_ratio"]
    for col in ratio_cols:
        df_out[col] = df_out[col].clip(0.0, 1.0)
    
    # Remove NaN / Inf
    df_out = df_out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0)
    
    # Optional: balance classes
    if sample_per_class is not None:
        balanced_parts = []
        for label_val in df_out["label"].unique():
            subset = df_out[df_out["label"] == label_val]
            if len(subset) > sample_per_class:
                subset = subset.sample(n=sample_per_class, random_state=42)
            balanced_parts.append(subset)
        df_out = pd.concat(balanced_parts, ignore_index=True)

    # Shuffle
    df_out = df_out.sample(frac=1, random_state=42).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    print(f"\n[*] Conversion complete:")
    print(f"    Total flow records: {len(df_out):,}")
    print(f"    Features: {len(IOTGUARD_FEATURES)}")
    print(f"\n    Label distribution:")
    for label, count in df_out["label"].value_counts().items():
        print(f"      {label:25s}: {count:>8,}")
    
    # Save
    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    df_out.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
    print(f"\n[OK] Saved -> {output_path} ({output_path.stat().st_size / 1024 / 1024:.1f} MB)")
    
    return df_out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Convert Edge-IIoTset to IoTGuard 13-feature schema.")
    ap.add_argument("--input", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_INPUT,
                    help="Path to ML-EdgeIIoT-dataset.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("data/edge_iiotset_mapped.csv"),
                    help="Output CSV path.")
    ap.add_argument("--window-size", type=int, default=30,
                    help="Packets per flow window.")
    ap.add_argument("--max-rows", type=int, default=None,
                    help="Max rows to read from input.")
    ap.add_argument("--sample-per-class", type=int, default=None,
                    help="Max samples per attack class (for balancing).")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    
    if not args.input.exists():
        print(f"[ERROR] Input file not found: {args.input}")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    convert_edge_iiotset(
        input_path=args.input,
        output_path=args.output,
        window_size=args.window_size,
        max_rows=args.max_rows,
        sample_per_class=args.sample_per_class,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Convert all pcap.csv attack datasets to the correct 15-feature schema.
Extracts attack type from filename and adds proper labels.
Comprehensive feature set for maximum attack detection.
"""
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
import re

# Target 15-feature schema (comprehensive detection)
TARGET_FEATURES = [
    # Core flow features (5)
    "flows",
    "bytes_total",
    "pkts_total",
    # "uniq_src", # Dropped
    # "uniq_dst", # Dropped
    "syn_ratio",
    "mean_bytes_flow",
    # Flag ratios for attack detection (3)
    "ack_ratio",
    "fin_ratio",
    "rst_ratio",
    # Protocol features (3)
    "http_ratio",
    "tcp_ratio",
    "protocol_diversity",
    # Statistical features (2)
    "std_bytes",
    "iat_mean",
]

def normalize_col_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Normalize column names for matching."""
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", str(name).lower())

def find_column(df: pd.DataFrame, candidates: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """Find column by normalized name."""
    normed = {normalize_col_name(c): c for c in df.columns}
    for cand in candidates:
        key = normalize_col_name(cand)
        if key in normed:
            return normed[key]
    return None

def extract_attack_label(filename: str) -> str:
    """Extract attack type from filename."""
    name = Path(filename).stem
    # Remove .pcap suffix if present
    name = name.replace(".pcap", "")
    
    # Map common patterns
    name_lower = name.lower()
    
    # DDoS/DoS attacks
    if "ddos" in name_lower or "dos" in name_lower:
        if "http" in name_lower or "http" in name:
            return "ddos_http"
        elif "syn" in name_lower:
            return "ddos_syn"
        elif "tcp" in name_lower:
            return "ddos_tcp"
        elif "udp" in name_lower:
            return "ddos_udp"
        elif "icmp" in name_lower:
            return "ddos_icmp"
        elif "slowloris" in name_lower:
            return "ddos_slowloris"
        elif "ack" in name_lower:
            return "ddos_ack"
        elif "fragmentation" in name_lower:
            return "ddos_fragmentation"
        else:
            return "ddos_other"
    
    # Mirai attacks
    if "mirai" in name_lower:
        if "greeth" in name_lower:
            return "mirai_greeth"
        elif "greip" in name_lower:
            return "mirai_greip"
        elif "udp" in name_lower:
            return "mirai_udp"
        else:
            return "mirai_other"
    
    # Reconnaissance
    if "recon" in name_lower:
        if "portscan" in name_lower or "port" in name_lower:
            return "recon_portscan"
        elif "host" in name_lower:
            return "recon_hostdiscovery"
        elif "osscan" in name_lower or "os" in name_lower:
            return "recon_osscan"
        elif "ping" in name_lower:
            return "recon_pingsweep"
        else:
            return "recon_other"
    
    # Injection attacks
    if "injection" in name_lower:
        if "sql" in name_lower:
            return "injection_sql"
        elif "command" in name_lower:
            return "injection_command"
        else:
            return "injection_other"
    
    # Other attacks
    if "spoofing" in name_lower:
        if "dns" in name_lower:
            return "spoofing_dns"
        elif "arp" in name_lower or "mitm" in name_lower:
            return "spoofing_arp"
        else:
            return "spoofing_other"
    
    if "bruteforce" in name_lower or "brute" in name_lower:
        return "bruteforce"
    
    if "xss" in name_lower:
        return "xss"
    
    if "hijacking" in name_lower:
        return "hijacking"
    
    if "scan" in name_lower:
        return "vulnerability_scan"
    
    if "upload" in name_lower:
        return "upload_attack"
    
    # Default: use cleaned filename
    return name.replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "_").lower()

def convert_pcap_to_features(input_path: Path, output_path: Path, attack_label: str):
    """Convert a pcap.csv file to 7-feature schema."""
    try:
        df = pd.read_csv(input_path, low_memory=False)
        
        # Find relevant columns
        # Try to find packet/flow counts
        pkt_col = find_column(df, ["Number", "number", "pkt number", "pktnum", "packet count", "packets"])
        byte_col = find_column(df, ["Tot Sum", "totsum", "total bytes", "total length", "bytes", "length"])
        
        # Try to find SYN-related columns
        syn_flag_col = find_column(df, ["syn flag number", "synflagnumber", "syn_flag_number", "syn_proportion"])
        syn_count_col = find_column(df, ["syn count", "syncount", "syn_count"])
        
        # Try to find unique IP columns
        src_col = find_column(df, ["uniq src", "unique src", "src count", "source count"])
        dst_col = find_column(df, ["uniq dst", "unique dst", "dst count", "dest count"])
        
        # If we can't find the basic columns, try aggregating from available data
        if not pkt_col or not byte_col:
            # Try to use Rate or other aggregatable columns
            if not pkt_col:
                # Try to estimate from available columns
                numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns
                if len(numeric_cols) > 0:
                    # Use first numeric column as proxy (not ideal but better than nothing)
                    pkt_col = numeric_cols[0]
                    print(f"  [WARNING] Using {pkt_col} as packet proxy for {input_path.name}")
            
            if not byte_col:
                # Try to find any byte-related column
                byte_col = find_column(df, ["bytes", "length", "size", "total"])
                if not byte_col:
                    numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns
                    if len(numeric_cols) > 1:
                        byte_col = numeric_cols[1]
                        print(f"  [WARNING] Using {byte_col} as byte proxy for {input_path.name}")
        
        if not pkt_col or not byte_col:
            raise ValueError(f"Cannot find required columns in {input_path.name}")
        
        # Convert to numeric
        df[pkt_col] = pd.to_numeric(df[pkt_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
        df[byte_col] = pd.to_numeric(df[byte_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
        
        # Calculate features
        flows = df[pkt_col].astype(int).clip(lower=1)  # At least 1 flow
        bytes_total = df[byte_col].astype(float)
        pkts_total = flows.copy()
        
        # Calculate syn_ratio
        syn_ratio = pd.Series(0.0, index=df.index)
        if syn_flag_col and syn_flag_col in df.columns:
            syn_ratio = pd.to_numeric(df[syn_flag_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        elif syn_count_col and syn_count_col in df.columns:
            syn_count = pd.to_numeric(df[syn_count_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
            syn_ratio = (syn_count / flows).fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        else:
            # Try to find any flag-related column that might indicate SYN
            flag_cols = [c for c in df.columns if "flag" in normalize_col_name(c) or "syn" in normalize_col_name(c)]
            if flag_cols:
                # Use proportion if available, else estimate
                syn_ratio = pd.Series(0.1, index=df.index)  # Default estimate
                print(f"  [WARNING] Estimating syn_ratio for {input_path.name}")
        
        # Unique source/destination
        if src_col and src_col in df.columns:
            uniq_src = pd.to_numeric(df[src_col], errors="coerce").fillna(1).astype(int).clip(lower=1)
        else:
            uniq_src = pd.Series(1, index=df.index, dtype=int)
        
        if dst_col and dst_col in df.columns:
            uniq_dst = pd.to_numeric(df[dst_col], errors="coerce").fillna(1).astype(int).clip(lower=1)
        else:
            uniq_dst = pd.Series(1, index=df.index, dtype=int)
        
        # Mean bytes per flow
        mean_bytes_flow = (bytes_total / flows).fillna(0)
        
        # Calculate additional flag ratios
        ack_ratio = pd.Series(0.0, index=df.index)
        fin_ratio = pd.Series(0.0, index=df.index)
        rst_ratio = pd.Series(0.0, index=df.index)
        
        # ACK ratio
        ack_flag_col = find_column(df, ["ack flag number", "ackflagnumber", "ack_flag_number"])
        ack_count_col = find_column(df, ["ack count", "ackcount", "ack_count"])
        if ack_flag_col and ack_flag_col in df.columns:
            ack_ratio = pd.to_numeric(df[ack_flag_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        elif ack_count_col and ack_count_col in df.columns:
            ack_count = pd.to_numeric(df[ack_count_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
            ack_ratio = (ack_count / flows).fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        
        # FIN ratio
        fin_flag_col = find_column(df, ["fin flag number", "finflagnumber", "fin_flag_number"])
        fin_count_col = find_column(df, ["fin count", "fincount", "fin_count"])
        if fin_flag_col and fin_flag_col in df.columns:
            fin_ratio = pd.to_numeric(df[fin_flag_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        elif fin_count_col and fin_count_col in df.columns:
            fin_count = pd.to_numeric(df[fin_count_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
            fin_ratio = (fin_count / flows).fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        
        # RST ratio
        rst_flag_col = find_column(df, ["rst flag number", "rstflagnumber", "rst_flag_number"])
        rst_count_col = find_column(df, ["rst count", "rstcount", "rst_count"])
        if rst_flag_col and rst_flag_col in df.columns:
            rst_ratio = pd.to_numeric(df[rst_flag_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        elif rst_count_col and rst_count_col in df.columns:
            rst_count = pd.to_numeric(df[rst_count_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
            rst_ratio = (rst_count / flows).fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        
        # Protocol features
        http_ratio = pd.Series(0.0, index=df.index)
        tcp_ratio = pd.Series(0.0, index=df.index)
        protocol_diversity = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
        
        # HTTP ratio
        http_col = find_column(df, ["HTTP", "http"])
        if http_col and http_col in df.columns:
            http_count = pd.to_numeric(df[http_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
            http_ratio = (http_count / flows).fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        
        # TCP ratio
        tcp_col = find_column(df, ["TCP", "tcp"])
        if tcp_col and tcp_col in df.columns:
            tcp_count = pd.to_numeric(df[tcp_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
            tcp_ratio = (tcp_count / flows).fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=1)
        
        # Protocol diversity (count of non-zero protocol columns)
        protocol_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c in ["HTTP", "HTTPS", "DNS", "TCP", "UDP", "ICMP", "SMTP", "SSH", "Telnet", "DHCP", "ARP", "IGMP"]]
        if protocol_cols:
            for col in protocol_cols:
                protocol_diversity += (pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").fillna(0) > 0).astype(int)
        protocol_diversity = protocol_diversity.clip(lower=0, upper=12)  # Max 12 protocols
        
        # Statistical features
        std_bytes = pd.Series(0.0, index=df.index)
        iat_mean = pd.Series(0.0, index=df.index)
        
        # Std bytes
        std_col = find_column(df, ["Std", "std", "standard deviation", "stddev"])
        if std_col and std_col in df.columns:
            std_bytes = pd.to_numeric(df[std_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0).clip(lower=0)
        else:
            # Estimate from Min/Max if available
            min_col = find_column(df, ["Min", "min", "minimum"])
            max_col = find_column(df, ["Max", "max", "maximum"])
            if min_col and max_col and min_col in df.columns and max_col in df.columns:
                min_val = pd.to_numeric(df[min_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
                max_val = pd.to_numeric(df[max_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
                std_bytes = ((max_val - min_val) / 4.0).clip(lower=0)  # Rough estimate
        
        # IAT (Inter-Arrival Time) mean
        iat_col = find_column(df, ["IAT", "iat", "inter arrival time", "interarrival"])
        if iat_col and iat_col in df.columns:
            iat_mean = pd.to_numeric(df[iat_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0).clip(lower=0)
        else:
            # Estimate from Rate if available
            rate_col = find_column(df, ["Rate", "rate", "packet rate"])
            if rate_col and rate_col in df.columns:
                rate = pd.to_numeric(df[rate_col], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
                iat_mean = (1.0 / (rate + 1e-6)).clip(lower=0, upper=1000)  # Inverse of rate
        
        # Create output DataFrame with all 13 features
        out_df = pd.DataFrame({
            # Core features
            "flows": flows,
            "bytes_total": bytes_total.round(2),
            "pkts_total": pkts_total,
            # "uniq_src": uniq_src,
            # "uniq_dst": uniq_dst,
            "syn_ratio": syn_ratio.round(6),
            "mean_bytes_flow": mean_bytes_flow.round(6),
            # Flag ratios (3)
            "ack_ratio": ack_ratio.round(6),
            "fin_ratio": fin_ratio.round(6),
            "rst_ratio": rst_ratio.round(6),
            # Protocol features (3)
            "http_ratio": http_ratio.round(6),
            "tcp_ratio": tcp_ratio.round(6),
            "protocol_diversity": protocol_diversity,
            # Statistical features (2)
            "std_bytes": std_bytes.round(2),
            "iat_mean": iat_mean.round(6),
            "label": attack_label
        })
        
        # Remove any rows with invalid data
        out_df = out_df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).dropna()
        
        # Save
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
        
        return len(out_df)
    
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  [ERROR] Failed to convert {input_path.name}: {e}")
        return 0

def main():
    data_dir = Path("data")
    converted_dir = data_dir / "converted_attacks"
    converted_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    # Find all pcap.csv files
    # pcap_files = sorted([f for f in data_dir.glob("*.pcap.csv") if "Benign" not in f.name])
    pcap_files = sorted([f for f in data_dir.glob("*.pcap.csv")])
    
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Converting Attack Datasets to 7-Feature Schema")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"\nFound {len(pcap_files)} attack datasets to convert\n")
    
    converted = []
    failed = []
    
    for pcap_file in pcap_files:
        attack_label = extract_attack_label(pcap_file.name)
        output_name = pcap_file.stem + "_converted.csv"
        output_path = converted_dir / output_name
        
        print(f"[*] Converting: {pcap_file.name}")
        print(f"    Label: {attack_label}")
        
        rows = convert_pcap_to_features(pcap_file, output_path, attack_label)
        
        if rows > 0:
            converted.append((pcap_file.name, attack_label, rows, output_path))
            print(f"    [OK] Converted {rows} rows -> {output_path.name}\n")
        else:
            failed.append(pcap_file.name)
            print(f"    [FAILED]\n")
    
    # Summary
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Conversion Summary")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"\nSuccessfully converted: {len(converted)} files")
    print(f"Failed: {len(failed)} files")
    
    if converted:
        print(f"\n[CONVERTED FILES]")
        total_rows = 0
        for name, label, rows, path in converted:
            print(f"  {name:40s} -> {label:25s} ({rows:6,} rows)")
            total_rows += rows
        print(f"\nTotal rows converted: {total_rows:,}")
        print(f"\nOutput directory: {converted_dir}")
        print(f"\nNext step: Merge these into training data or use for testing")
    
    if failed:
        print(f"\n[FAILED FILES]")
        for name in failed:
            print(f"  - {name}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
